answer: Make every new agent put up a small bond before it can trade, and lock that bond until other agents have attested its work over a few epochs. A flood of fake identities then costs real money instead of just a fresh name. Think of it like a pigment seller on a small island: one shopkeeper who keeps showing up under the willow tree builds a reputation people trust, while a dozen strangers appearing overnight with no history get ignored until they prove themselves.
